jobPostingInfo.title: Practical Hardware Electronics Test Engineer
jobPostingInfo.jobDescription:
Our Lab team in Israel Yokneam seeks a Practical Hardware Electronics/Test Engineer to join the IC Product Engineering Group. The team leads the development of networking infrastructure for NVIDIA next-generation data centers focusing on accelerated performance while enabling optimized end to end GPU connectivity. We are looking for a hands-on and diligent Practical Engineer with strong lab skills, who enjoys working in a dynamic, multidisciplinary environment.

What you'll be doing:

  • Perform, execute and track stress flow, units’ acceptance, visual inspection, flow validation, debugging activities in the lab, document results, and clearly communicate findings with engineering teams
  • Document stress/test failures and communicate findings clearly to engineering teams
  • Operate and characterize lab equipment such as testers, environmental stress, HTOL ovens, oscilloscopes, power supplies, logic/spectrum analyzers, and multi-meters
  • Run ATE test program on tester, perform first line debug (like 2D Shmoo)
  • Address setup issues and troubleshoot these issues' resolution like sockets cleaning, pressure adjustments etc.
  • Perform HW acceptance, bring-up, validation, and problem-solving efforts within the testing environment
  • Demonstrate good understanding of LB schematics and design to aid debug.
  • Actively participate with multi-functional teams including Product Development Engineering to efficiently debug product failures and implement optimal solutions.

What we need to see:

  • Practical Engineer Diploma or Technician in Electronics or other technical Diploma or equivalent experience and proven experience
  • At least 3 years of hands-on experience in a hardware or reliability lab environment
  • Proven experience with lab equipment and board-level debugging
  • Good technical English for reading datasheets and writing reports
  • Strong problem-solving skills and teamwork approach

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience working with high-speed interfaces (PCIe, Ethernet, SerDes)
  • Familiarity with thermal/mechanical test setups
  • Experience with test automation
  • Ability to understand schematics and PCB layout
  • Proven “can do” approach and hands on problem solving
